title: The Wolf in Sheep’s Clothing
originalTitle: The Wolf in Sheep’s Clothing · English
sourceAuthor: Aesop; selected and told anew by Joseph Jacobs
note: The public-domain text of “The Wolf in Sheep’s Clothing” is reproduced directly from this edition; page divisions are editorial. The cover and turning-point illustrations come from Project Gutenberg ebooks 39187 (images/i_039.jpg) and 19994 (images/i071_th.jpg). No suitable third source plate was found, so the ending is a new collection illustration in a historically appropriate ancient Mediterranean setting.

rights.basis: The 1894 source edition is identified as public domain in the United States by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: A disguised wolf strolls among a flock while shepherd dogs watch.
scenes: A Wolf found great difficulty in getting at the sheep owing to the vigilance of the shepherd and his dogs.
But one day it found the skin of a sheep that had been flayed and thrown aside, so it put it on over its own pelt and strolled down among the sheep.

The Lamb that belonged to the sheep, whose skin the Wolf was wearing, began to follow the Wolf in the Sheep’s clothing; so, leading the Lamb a little apart, he soon made a meal off her, and for some time he succeeded in deceiving the sheep, and enjoying hearty meals.

pageArt.alt: The wolf pulls a discarded fleece over its dark pelt.
A lamb follows the sheep-clad wolf away from the unsuspecting flock.
